params.caption.prompt: Six minute southern blues rock album closer with a heavy swaggering half time groove, opening with a clean chiming descending guitar figure on a bright single coil bridge pickup through a spring reverb tank with no drums, then the full trio crashing in, foreground electric guitar through a rocking wah pedal and a germanium fuzz into a cranked hundred watt stack with natural power tube breakup and controlled feedback, heavy finger vibrato, wide whole step bends, percussive sixteenth note rhythm scratching behind the beat, verses rolling on a single dominant seventh chord with a country rock lilt, choruses lifting on a five six one movement with a borrowed flat seventh, warm round bass playing melodic countermelody instead of roots, loose powerful live drums with a deep tuned floor tom, splashy hand hammered cymbals and a fat backbeat snare, tambourine, warm plainspoken male baritone lead vocal, slightly nasal, drawling and conversational, close miked with short slap echo, shouted double tracked chorus, long extended guitar jam outro with feedback and a slow fade, humid and unhurried turning triumphant, E Mixolydian with blues thirds, vintage analog tape production with real room bleed. crazygecko
params.caption.lyrics:
[Intro - clean chiming guitar figure, no drums]

[Intro - wah guitar and full trio enter]

[Verse 1 - rolling, one chord groove]
Been gone long enough to lose my drawl
Got it back the second I stepped down
Same man selling peanuts by the depot
Same dog asleep on the same hot ground

[Verse 2 - rolling]
Twelve years and a borrowed suitcase
Nothing in it worth the freight
Reckon nobody's fixing to forgive me
Reckon I'm not fixing to wait

[Chorus - heavy, wah and fuzz]
TELL THE RIVER I'M COMING
Tell it slow and tell it plain
Been a long time gone to yonder
Come to stand out in the rain
TELL THE RIVER I'M COMING
Same clothes and the same crooked name
Every road I ever ruined
Runs back through here all the same

[Verse 3 - rolling]
Aunt Cleo's still got the kettle
Still won't let a man sit down
Says the Lord don't keep a ledger
Says the town keeps one around

[Chorus - heavy, wah and fuzz]
TELL THE RIVER I'M COMING
Tell it slow and tell it plain
Been a long time gone to yonder
Come to stand out in the rain
TELL THE RIVER I'M COMING
Same clothes and the same crooked name
Every road I ever ruined
Runs back through here all the same

[Verse 4 - rolling, quieter]
Mailbox got my name misspelled
Been that way for twenty years
Much obliged to whoever painted
Anything at all out here

[Guitar Solo - long, wah and fuzz, full trio, building]

[Bridge - half time, heavy]
I don't aim to be forgiven
I aim to be understood
Difference ain't worth arguing
When the water's up for good

[Chorus - heavy, full band]
TELL THE RIVER I'M COMING
Tell it slow and tell it plain
Been a long time gone to yonder
Come to stand out in the rain

[Chorus - heavy, doubled and shouted]
TELL THE RIVER I'M COMING
Same clothes and the same crooked name
Every road I ever ruined
Runs back through here all the same

[Outro - extended guitar jam, feedback, long slow fade]
params.file.name: Tell the River I'm Coming
